subject: Pilot: SFTP export retention bridge — conditional short-term keep & purge sequencing
messages:
From: Maria Kovacs <maria.kovacs@mediscan.health>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.ai, kimberly.park@redwood.ai
Cc: security@mediscan.health
Date: Thu, 4 Sep 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Temporary evidence keep for EU audit — short-term request

Hi Jonas / Kimberly,

We have a regulator-led inquiry in the EU that requires us to preserve a narrow set of telemetry and request logs for a two-week window while our auditors validate a chain of events. Can Redwood do a temporary retain on the nightly SFTP exports from the eu-west-1 bucket for the window 2025-09-05 -> 2025-09-19?

Specifics: we only need the pipeline-exported logs for three API keys (listed in the attached manifest) and the SFTP delivery receipts. We understand this is an exception to your standard purge cadence — happy to provide a signed DPA addendum / limited-scope access request.

Please let us know what evidence (export checksum, audit logs) you can provide and the specific purge sequencing so we can confirm with our legal team.

Thanks,
Maria Kovacs
Head of Compliance
Mediscan Health
[attachment: mediscan_sftp_manifest.csv (text/csv)]

From: jonas.weber@redwood.ai
To: Maria Kovacs <maria.kovacs@mediscan.health>
Cc: kimberly.park@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 4 Sep 2025 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Temporary evidence keep for EU audit — short-term request

Maria — thanks for the clear ask and the manifest. We can support a scoped, temporary retention carveout for the SFTP exports, with the following constraints and deliverables: 

- Scope: only the three API key directories named in your manifest and the SFTP delivery receipts for the specified dates. No additional datasets will be retained.
- Window: we can hold the nightly exports for 14 days (2025-09-05 00:00 UTC -> 2025-09-19 23:59 UTC). After the window the purge will run in a staggered sequence described below.
- Evidence we can provide: MD5 checksums for each exported file, SFTP delivery logs, and a system audit trail showing the temporary retain flag.
- Controls: access to retained files will be limited to Mediscan named contacts + Redwood Legal/Compliance; we will not surface retained files to other customers.

Next steps I need from you:
1) Confirm the exact SFTP manifest rows to retain (I pulled the attached but want sign-off).
2) Provide the signed limited-scope DPA addendum (Kimberly — I’m looping you here).
3) Confirm whether you require an immutable snapshot (WORM) or a soft-retain with deletion after the 14-day window.

Proposed purge sequencing (high level):
- Day 0 (2025-09-20 03:00 UTC): move staged files to a short-term quarantine bucket with a retention tag.
- Day 0+1: run checksum verification and produce evidence bundle (checksums + delivery logs).
- Day 0+2: apply purge job that deletes files in batches by API-key prefix to avoid I/O spikes.
- All steps logged and a final purge report produced.

Kimberly/Laura — can Legal/Operations sign the addendum and confirm the retention mode (immutable vs soft)? Aditya — can infra confirm SFTP export TTL change is low-risk and share ETA for the quarantine job?

-Jonas
Senior Manager, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: kimberly.park@redwood.ai
To: Maria Kovacs <maria.kovacs@mediscan.health>
Cc: jonas.weber@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai, Paul Turner <paul.turner@acme-legal.com>
Date: Thu, 4 Sep 2025 13:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Temporary evidence keep for EU audit — limited-scope DPA addendum

Maria / Paul — thanks. Legal is OK to approve a limited-scope DPA addendum for a short-term retention carveout provided Mediscan signs the addendum and confirms:

- Purpose limitation: the retained files will only be used for regulator evidence and will be deleted after the agreed window.
- Access list: provide named Mediscan contacts (email + role) who may request exports.
- Data export controls: confirm SFTP host, IP allowlist, and whether Mediscan requires an encrypted container.

I attached a one-page instruction packet for the evidence export and a DocuSign link for the addendum. Once signed we will treat this as an approved exception and proceed with the staging plan Jonas outlined.

Attachments: evidence_export_instructions.pdf (application/pdf)
DocuSign: https://docusign.net/ember/sign?token=0a1b2c3d4e

Please sign and return by EOD Friday (2025-09-05) to avoid delaying the auditor window.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Head of Privacy & Legal
Redwood Inference

> From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>

> To: jonas.weber@redwood.ai, kimberly.park@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai
> Subject: Technical plan for SFTP export quarantine and purge
>
> Team — tech details below for implementation once we have a signed addendum. Sharing here so Maria sees the sequencing.
>
> Implementation notes:
> - On sign-off we will flip a per-export metadata flag (temporary_retain=true) for the three API-key prefixes. That prevents downstream retention jobs from pruning the set.
> - Nightly export process will still run and place files in the eu-west-1 export bucket. We will run a scheduled job at 02:00 UTC that copies flagged files to a quarantine bucket (eu-west-1-quarantine). The copy operation will compute an MD5 and store it in the manifest.
> - Quarantine bucket will have object lifecycle disabled for 21 days so there is headroom to produce evidence. Purge will be manual-triggered after the evidence bundle is validated.
> - Purge job: delete by prefix in 6-minute windows with a 1-minute cooldown to avoid impacting SFTP throughput. We will emit metrics to the Redwood Console and create a final purge_report.json in the evidence folder.
>
> Required from Mediscan: SFTP public key for the delivery host (to verify receipts) and the final list of named accessors.
>
> Attachments: mediscan_sftp_manifest.csv
>
> I will schedule the quarantine job for 2025-09-20 02:00 UTC assuming we get the signed addendum.
>
> -Aditya (Infra)
